system.biography:
Part lion, part elephant, part horse. Huge, often mistaken for terrain features until the hill wakes up, shakes off centuries of dust and begins a cumbersome rampage.

Climbable

Huge person-sized baboons. Have their own language, culture and laws. Local leader is always their oldest living member. Worship celestial bodies and value trade in tobacco and candy, which they adore but can’t make for themselves. Pity human beings as malformed cousins, don't see them as equals. Can learn Mystic Martial Arts, those that do become kings and emperors of their kind.

Human-Esque

Herd animal; horns, hooves, you get the idea. Stats can be adjusted slightly to accommodate anything elk-like (Like deer or whatever; the exact genus of elk-like-creature is not a focus for this game). Can also be used for horses.

Massive crabs with iron-hard shells. Solitary, sometimes intelligent, often festooned with graffiti. Some in the deep dunes are said to be as big as battleships, but certainly that’s a myth…

Devil crabs are often tamed while still young and used as war animals by aspiring warlords. They can support Ordnance weapons and are comparable to living tanks

Mystical horn-dogs, friends with fire. Decadent to excess, they’re powerful sorcerers and prone to bribery. Favor smoking jackets and other attire that rides the border between elegant and sleazy. Shapeshifters, they look a little like tiger-people in their base form.

Human-Esque

The six-armed shadow of a dead ninja; hunts those who stray too far from crowds.

Ghostly
Burn bright in the forests of the night, if Blake is to be trusted. Big striped murder-machines, maneaters from myth but they’re real and hungry and just, so goddamn radical.

Life sucks and then you die. Then, it sucks even more once a combination of diabolic magic and radioactive waste reanimates your corpse and with an unceasing hunger for living flesh.

Human-Esque

An army of rats, worms or other nasties twisted and mangled together into a single, hideous super-vermin.

Swarm: Area
Watermelon-sized, ebony-skinned bees. They have the most venomous sting on the planet and their royal jelly is said to cure any disease.

Bhuut, Hungry Ghosts, and other strange nasties. Died so long ago they’ve lost all traces of humanity. Wild and hungry and impossible to kill except in specific and largely unknown ways.

Ghostly

Equal parts lion, scorpion and bat; surprisingly a product of the mythic and banished past rather than the horrifying mutative present. As cunning as a serial killer and twice as hungry for human meat, the manticore is ravenous beyond the appetite of any mortal predator. It devours entire villages at once, laying gorged and contented with a belly as full as a graveyard. It’s scorpion-like tail can launch venomous spines and it has three rows of teeth, as though you didn’t have enough problems. It can, but rarely does, speak human languages with it’s eerily human face.

Ferocity: 12

Health: 12

Size: 6

Capabilities: Fly and move at Agility Rank 3 (Giant Bat Wings).

Powerful fore paws: +1 Rank to two attacks per round.

Barbed tail: +1d10 Initiative and Reach as a spear. Envenom a single strike per round, Virulence 3. Can fire Ranged 1/round.

Charge Attack: Berserk

Set Cost: 4 sets.

Rank: 5

Effect: Attack every target in the same Area in a fury of claws, wings and scorpion stings. If the manticore is airborne when you launch this strike, it gains Advantage.

A vision, dream or other hallucination that roils over your consciousness and won’t leave until it’s dilemma has been resolved.

This changes the Field into a completely different Field. This isn’t “real”, it’s a psychic mirage, but the characters interact with it as though it’s real.

Choose or randomly select a Struggle from the Lores section (p.248); the vision is about that dilemma in microcosm. The characters are “trapped” within this hallucination until they resolve its central dilemma (whatever you decide that is; usually it manifests as a moral choice of some variety).

  • Mortals fall unconscious while trapped within the quest, but Lone Wolf Fists instinctively meditate in the lotus position while incapacitated.

  • In the material world, one Real-Time Scene passes no matter how long the vision takes to resolve. If anything disturbs the characters, even slightly, while they remain in the vision, it is dispelled and they immediately awaken.

  • Even though the vision is fake, any Kharma earned during the quest are very real.

Something like sentient viruses and living, elemental assassins from Heaven. Seek out earthly immortals to annihilate; take the form of a multi-armed god of lightning, fire or wind. They devour you from the inside-out by burning through your Prana meridians if they catch you.

Angel

Horrible amalgam of man, machine, animal or something wholly and unwholesomely unique. Eat meat, lots of it.

Human-Esque
Apex predators and kings of the sky. Make totally radical pets.

Pretender god. Really powerful, but they know they’re not the real deal and it eats at them. Cannot gain power from worship, but they feel it legitimizes them so they crave it anyway. Lack a divine decree, but often practice elementally-aligned Mystic Martial Arts so that they can pretend that the universe obeys their whims. Immortal, they are hunted relentlessly by the Sanzai.

Spirit
The nastier of the prehistoric beasts. Scaly, no feathers on these dudes. Maybe engineered species, it’s not clear where they came from post-armageddon.

Just really big, intelligent animals. They can speak the

language of spirits, which is similar to telepathy. Radically

racist against humans, or “man-apes” as they’re derisively

known.

Uses Effort instead of Ferocity. Effort 8-14, Health = Effort.
The nastier of the prehistoric beasts. Scaly, no feathers on these dudes. Maybe engineered species, it’s not clear where they came from post-armageddon.

Floating head trailing its former organs. Eats flesh grows gigantic as it continues to devour people. The elder ones are as big as a blimp.

Demon

Your Jaguars and Lions, Rhinos if they’re mad enough. Sometimes you just want to punch a hippo in their big, stupid face.

Ferocity = 5-10, Health = 5-10, Size = 5-6

Corpses inhabited by an enlightened ghost. Some are knowledgeable and demand a dark price for their tutelage. Some are just soul-hungry assholes; it’s incredibly hard to tell which you’re dealing with at first.

Demon

Any deceased Lone Wolf Fist who is slain with hate in their heart can arise as a Vetala Their ghost, battened on sin and Prana, flees into the nearest corpse and reanimates it during the next New Moon. The corpse has all the traits they had in life, but is usually rotting or mutilated. It follows the same Corpse-Body rules as those in the Art of the Sorcerer (p.126), except that the ghost within is vulnerable to exorcism and its damage cannot be repaired through any means due to the soul-body connection’s less integrated nature.

If their corpse-form is ever irreparably destroyed, the Vetala must flee to another nearby corpse within the same Field or be swept up into the Kharmic Wheel and reincarnated.

The Vetala have an Aura of Malfeasance that surrounds them, polluting the local Dharma. This causes sickness in livestock, bad fortune, miscarriages, famine, pestilence, and all other manner of awful things to transpire. This aura affects everything within the same Field as a Misfortune Hardship every Campaign Arc.

If the Vetala was Degree 8 or higher in life, then the Field they’re in suffers a Disaster Hardship every Arc, and the surrounding Tract is affected by their aura as a Misfortune Hardship. Not every Mystic Martial Artist who dies with a soul poisoned by hate arises as a Vetala; the specifics of the misfortune are obscure. The practice of honoring a slain foe and holding a properly respectful funeral always keeps a Vetala from arising, so it is a common custom within the martial world.

Just a giant creature made out of random debris and transformed by psychic will into a being of destructive might.

Mechanical Being

Cheaply produced genetic servants; big dumb and ugly.

Human-Esque

Element-themed, giant lion/dog monster. Dye their hair and get piercings: they’re “so done” with their cosmic duty to protect sacred sites. They will kill you if you defile or attempt to defile them, but they don’t try to justify this, even to themselves.

Draconic horse or equine dragon; Supposedly emissaries from heaven sent to steward the green world, but by turns benevolent and hostile. They’re rarely seen, but those who encounter one are changed forever.

After an Atomic Jiangshi has eaten the flesh of 1000 mortals, the accumulated flesh metastasises within their bodies as a Chakra Tumor, a sort of cancerous, inverted Chakra that putrefies cosmic essence and poisons the word. Such scions of atrocity are referred to as Ascendant Jiangshi or Scholars of Hell. They are more intelligent and powerful than their lesser cousins, possessing 3 Effort rather than Ferocity, as well as 3 Health. If they continue to devour human flesh, they continue to achieve a new metamorphosis for every 1000 lives destroyed.

As they grow more powerful, they grow Chakra Tumors, each one able to convert toxicified element-energy. Jiangshi evolving in this way are represented by the character creation mechanics; they are not mortal, so have no need for food, rest, water or air, surviving on Prana absorbed through devoured flesh alone. They are universally “Enlightened” style heroes, and begin their existence with a Chakra Tumor suitable to their climate in addition to their Hell Chakra. Although the martial styles they practice are ancient, lost and esoteric fighting arts of hell, they can be approximated by taking a blend of the two Shadow Viper martial styles. As scholars of hell, they know a single Gupt Kala and often learn another as they grow in power. Finally, they may use any version of the Element Spell for which they have an elementally appropriate Chakra.

Human-Esque

This is merely a sample statblock of a Degree 1 Ascendant Jiangshi. Should one be more persistent in your campaign or be of higher level, advance him in degree yourself.

People-eating freaks, what’s not to love?

Human-Esque

Have Ferocity instead of Effort (initially).
Gigantic, heavy, and packing enough destructive force to topple buildings in a single swipe of their claws. Come in numerous forms, eat copious amounts of raw flesh and bone.

Inhabit the once-holy waters of formerly sacred ponds, lakes and shrines. Can grow as big as a submarine, with two awkward teeth capable of penetrating steel and the hungering patience of an indolent god.
Massive insects, as big as dobermans. Eat flesh, spray organic acid, fly. If nature could give you the middle finger, this is how she would do it.

Hulking, death-puking artifact of war.

Mechanical Being

Air-elemental beings; also horn-dogs, but way tsundere about it. Favor bazookas, live on top floor aviaries to be close to the sky. Some become drug addicts and form violent gangs.

Human-Esque

Either a lot of little demons or one gigantic one, manifests as slimy tentacles that emerge from shadows to rip apart stray cats and drag people to unspeakable doom.

Ghostly, Demon

A dream predator, brought to life by a psychically-opened rift between the dreaming world and the real.

Ghostly

Mostly prey animals or simians like gibbon-men or llamamen. Reclusive, but they love to trade for stuff like tobacco and chocolate. Nobody knows how to speak their crazy moon-language, but they seem to be able to communicate with plants and spirits and have weird deals with both.

Human-Esque

Ghost-Men. Technically dead nomads, they can be valuable traders. A given tribe (16-ish, or 3d10) wishes for a specific good and travels a specific route, and they trade handsomely if you can figure out what they want (you just have to leave it out for them; it vanishes after they convene over it, no one knows where).

Ghostly

Human-Esque

Once gods of water, lakes, streams, seas and oceans, now a degenerate gaggle of wild-eyed lunatics.

Ghostly, Spirit

Powerful, immortal beings of disparate form and powers. Share in common that they were “deified” by one of the disasters that ended the previous world. Like to be worshiped and have a vested interest in keeping this world a terrible place.

Ghostly, Spirit

Chimerical amalgams of countless mystical beasts and creatures twisted together by mutating radiation. Devour foes whole, integrating their minds, bodies and powers into the megaform. Mere exposure causes hideous mutations.
Huge pitcher plants, sticky stalks that can grab and dissolve whole cows, pitcher plants with human skeletons floating in them, etc.

Enigmatic, weird-looking, but with rare or unique powers. They obey laws that everyone else forgot and never explain themselves, making them difficult to work with. Primeval spirits can teach their abilities, but are difficult to propitiate (or even communicate with!)

Ghostly, Spirit
The nastier of the prehistoric beasts. Scaly, no feathers on these dudes. Maybe engineered species, it’s not clear where they came from post-armageddon.
Eight-legged lion-snake-bird demons. Claim to be a god if they bother to speak. Usually just rampage into a place and eat everyone there. Actually hellacious philosophers when full.

Floating head trailing its former organs. Eats flesh grows gigantic as it continues to devour people. The elder ones are as big as a blimp.

Demon

Radiation-poisoned corpses, returned to hideous life by having a single note of a world-ending song lodged in their distended, putrid chakras. Intelligent, but utterly ravenous and ruthless.

Human-Esque

Musclebound, with ram-horns and screaming swords. Not subtle characters, they fought in the final wars and never got the order to stop.

Demon
A wizard of worms! Command legions of the wriggling, loathsome slime strings and want very unrealistic things from travels they encounter in the chthonic dark.

Towering scorpion-demons, once guardians of sacred sites but now hideously mutated and corrupted. Incredibly violent, they’re each the equivalent of an entire army. Often worshiped as gods, they rarely turn down the fresh meat of the sacrifices.
Four-armed, lion-headed crime lords. Their enforcers are called Heaven’s Law and are the most ruthless crime family in existence. Can forge masterwork swords.

Either a larval pestilence god or the result of divine degeneration in the eternal lightless depths, these protoplasmic monsters want blood to absorb through their mucusy, albino skin pores.

Ferocity: 25

Health: 25

Size: 7

Armor: 3 (Ineffective against Holy or Fire based attacks)

Demon, Spirit

Capabilities: Burrow through earth and stone or swim at a horrifying Rank 4. Vulnerable to Holy magic, but immune to all forms of corruption and decay (in fact, they thrive in highly toxic areas). Respire prayer from worship; every 10 devout followers grant 1 additional Prana per round.

Vampiric Skin: Against any grabbed foe, drain 3d10 damage’s worth of blood. Your weird body converts this to an equal amount of Prana
Whale-sized, carnivorous manta rays. Sleep under sand dunes in impossibly gigantic fevers.

A failed god, horrifying in appearance and power. Look like giant, malformed humans with extraneous bodily growths emerging and roiling across their tortured, near-divine physique. Incalculably powerful psychics.
Long, hideous yellow worms. Devour flesh and excrete acid.

Water-protection spirits gone rotten, they contaminate any liquid within miles. They look a bit like tiger-sized axolotl salamanders.

Spirit, Ghostly, Demon
"Everyone knows what a horse is" - Polish language dictionary.

An enlightened being who achieved immortality in a better age and is waiting for this one to burn itself out. Great at avoiding trouble and knows useful things, but tends to duck personal entanglement in your petty bullshit. After all, you’ll be dead in a few brief decades and it won’t matter.

While powerfully knowledgeable and generally the master of at least one form of Mystic Martial Arts, they are incredibly recalcitrant teachers and generally send “potential students” on outright suicide mission to rid themselves of the pests rather than teach them. They do honor their word if the student survives their insane trial, however.

Insane messengers of god. Wheels of brass with eyes, four-headed animal statues with lightning for hair, or even stranger shapes. Not hostile, exactly, but dangerous just by their nature; like toxic waste.

Angel

Weird, bulky, but unfailingly loyal and useful; machines from a less indecorous age.

Mechanical Being
Sharks, megalodons, and other huge toothy swimming monsters.

Disgusting, slimy inhabitants of the challenger deep. Some are quite huge and dangerous, and all of them conveniently ignore that “atmospheric pressure difference” hurdle due to a combination of good lobbying in the Heavenly courts from Sea Spirits and good ‘ol fashioned atomic mutation.

Ferocity: 10

Health: 8

Size: 5

Capabilities: Rank 2 slither with their amorphous form, can cling to surfaces that support part of its weight. Its pulsating, inconsistent form can contract into a space as small as a Room or expand to flood an entire Field.

Envelop: Rank 4, swallows a target and crushes a single unfortunate enemy. They remain enveloped and must endure crushing every round until they die or extricate themselves (Rank 4) 1/ Round.
Cruel, carnivorous, half-swan/crocodile, half lion. Stick prey on pikes outside their encampments.

The prisoner is any cool Spirit, Demon, or Immortal NPC you want to shove in an eternal prison. They can be unleashed only if you break them out of their Tech Prison.

Always want to be free, that would always be the worst possible scenario. Will absolutely make it worth your while.

Garbage-devouring, three-headed elephant monsters. Ebony black and tumorous. Claim they were cursed by Heaven for failing to save the world, but that's a dubious claim because they really enjoy their current lot and are also just such complete assholes.

A computer program with an axe to grind and a body of digital matter.

Ghostly

The upgraded, mostly-machine assassins that graduated from the lower tiers of lowlifedom. They’re the wrecking balls of the crime world, used for massive, targeted destruction.

Human-Esque

Alluring, intelligent, urbane; these demons are dangerous on a lot of levels.

Demon

Can use Ferocity for Heart actions and know the Art of the Courtier. Can learn any diabolical Mystic Martial Art; once they master enough to be Degree 1, they are treated as Cunning Heroes (as illustrated here) and trade Ferocity for Effort.

Goat-like people, nomads, instinctively know truth from lies.

Human-Esque

Temple guardians, statues, and gibbering madmen housed in bodies of immortal stone. If they had a purpose it’s immaterial now; they’re raving, murderous inmates and their asylums are the empty halls they were created to protect.

Mechanical Being
Huge, cannibal, tribal. Tend to hide despite their great ferocity.

A ball of eyes, or a rubber-limbed seductresses, or upsidedown heads with octopus tentacles for bodies; if you struggle to describe it, it's one of these.

Demon

Size: 1-4

system.description: Coats a Field in a white-hot discharge of Pranic energy, targeting an Area at (Achieved Rank) and burning the remaining Field at (Technique Rank). Counts as a Disaster Hardship.

Moves through its Stomp attacks, crashing each of its enormous legs down as it strides to its next destination.

Targets an Area within the same or an adjacent Field, deals a Rank 8 crushing blow as the foot smashes down (Leg).

The main body of the Yali is in the center of its legs, and they must move so as to allow it to walk. 4 such legs total, each moves 1/round. If 2 of them are destroyed, it can no longer walk, but continues to crawl until completely disabled.

system.powers:
The future is anyone’s game; people do regrettably have free will, and every problem in history is the result of that cosmic oversight. But the shape of the future is as concrete as the shape of the past, to those who understand how to see it. Some consult venerable poetry-texts, some stick hot pokers into tortoise shells, some toss the ol’ bones or draw from a deck of cards; some are just super-geniuses who figure it out. Whatever the method, these clairvoyants and savants make predictions that come true; where do you think all those ominous prophecies come from?

Uses the Senses Skill

Foretell Prophecy

You make predictions about the future, sensing the subtle twitches of the skein of fate. Prophecies might be somewhat broad and a touch vague, but they’re still true; or, rather, they’re the most likely shape the future will take.

To Foretell a Prophecy, first consult your preferred scrying equipment for ten minutes and craft a Prophecy.

You can (and should) be exceptionally weird and vague with the specifics of your prophecy, but you must articulate an Approach within it that allows cunning actors to exploit fate to their benefit (and avoid its perils!)

Prophecy Approach

The Approach is a statement of the form “The (Situation) must be approached in (Manner)”.

This will serve as the basis for judging whether people are acting in accordance with the Prophecy, similarly to a Dramatic Penalty in other Imbalances.

  • The Situation refers to a forthcoming Scene; it might be a battle, or an important ritual, or a social event; really, any specific event that’s going to happen within this Campaign Arc. While the scene lasts, the Prophecy effects everyone present and everyone whose actions influence the Scene. This means that even distant and indirect actors are affected while interacting with the prophesied event.

  • The Manner that it can be approached is prescriptive, like “cautiously” or “recklessly” or even something more esoteric like “reverently”. This is the trigger that is used to determine if a given character’s actions will be helped/hindered by the Prophecy. It can be as specific or broad as the Seer wishes; specificity will make it harder for foes to take advantage of the Prophecy, but will hinder the freedom of allies to pursue it creatively. Broader Manners allow for more flexibility, but risk the enemy benefiting from your Prophecy.

Next, take a Senses action to determine how accurate, broad and binding your new Prophecy turns out.

While in the Situation, characters must adhere to the Method of the Prophecy to claim its advantages, or avoid its penalties:

  • Rank 1: Adhering to the Manner prescribed for the Prophecy grants Advantage.

  • Rank 3: Additionally, ignoring the Manner causes Disadvantage.

  • Rank 6: Adhering additionally grants you +3 Effort per round. The GM has veto action against your actions while you enjoy this advantage; should a proposed action not harmonize with the Manner, you may not take that action.

  • Rank 9: Ignoring the Manner now additionally penalizes you -3 Effort each round. The GM must warn you, prior to committing to an action, if it will carry this auspicious sanction. If you cannot be penalized during this round, then you will lose 3 Effort in a future round/action of the GM’s choosing instead. Fate is cruel!

  • Rank 12: The scope of your Prophecy is broadened and deepened. It now applies more generally; the Prediction remains for the entire next Campaign Arc and influences everyone whose actions can be traced to the Situation during that time.

  • Rank 14+: Your Prophecy becomes permanent; it is inherited by the descendants of those involved in the situation, or the place it is foretold to occur, forever predicting those bloodlines or areas as auspicious places for the Situation to take place

Example Prophecies

Example Prophecy 1: “When the sun rises, everyone weeps. The air of winter is foul. The southern mountain has a bird and the north is fallen. When the cock crows, the sun shall set.”

Approach: The forthcoming battle in the Sword Peak Mountains must be approached subtly

Rank: 9

In this example, an indirect, stealthy or otherwise subtle approach to battle would be in accordance with the Approach.

Example Prophecy 2: “God is blind. The grass and trees grow downward. Positive and negative switch positions. Up is earth, and down is Heaven. Even the headless must wear crimson caps. Abusing authority, when will this end? A history of countless blunders will ensue”

Approach: The governance of Thankless Toil Providence must be approached frugally

Rank: 12

A more powerful Prophecy, this one applies to the entire next Campaign Arc, rather than a single scene. It essentially forbids ill-considered actions on the part of the rulers of the Thankless Toil Domain, forcing them to act uncharacteristically wise in their stewardship, the morons.

Predict Fate

You can foretell the fate of any person, place or thing, seeing their future as clearly as their present. These predictions are more concrete and limited in scope, so are much faster to generate; merely glance at your scrying tool and consider the subject and in a heartbeat the truth will reveal itself to you.

Predicting Fate creates an special kind of Imbalance, called a Prediction Imbalance. These are stranger than normal Imbalances, and can be applied to anything, not just people. They can also influence how others interact with the subject, rather than simply dictating how the subject will act.

To create a Prediciton Imbalance, use a Senses action and make a brief prediction using your chosen divination method, directed towards any a person, place or thing. You need not be able to perceive the target directly, as your divination sees their fate, rather than the subject itself.

Your prediction must take the form of: “(Subject) will (Prosper/Decline) if (Circumstance arises)”

  • For nonliving targets, the Rank of your action determines the Rank of the Prediction.

  • For living targets, they may defend against your prophesied doom with their own Senses action, subtracting their action from yours and taking Aggravation equal to the difference.

You may choose whether the target Prospers or Declines.

Prosper predictions allow the target to claim a Bonus if their actions this round/turn all adhere to the prophecy’s dictates.

Decline predictions enforce their Penalty unless their target adheres to the prophecy’s edicts this round/turn (in this way, it functions almost identically to a Dramatic Penalty)

Note that Predictions Imbalances need not adhere strictly to the “Subject will decline/prosper if circumstance” formula, they need merely contain a subject, action and direction of fortunes. So “Those who swear the Pumpkin-Stealing Oath will decline if they betray its dictates” works as well as “Those who break the Pumpkin-Stealing Oath shall suffer”

Prediction Imbalances

The Rank of these peculiar Imbalances determine how much of bonus/Penalty they enforce as well as how long they last;

  • Rank 3: +/-1 Effort, 1 Week

  • Rank 6: +/-2 Effort, 1 Month

  • Rank 9: +/-3 Effort, 1 Season/Arc

  • Rank 12: +/-4 Effort, 1 Year

  • Rank 14+: +/-5 Effort, Permanent

Prosper predictions award Effort bonuses, while Decline predictions enforce penalties. To claim a bonus, you must either act within or cause the described circumstance. To avoid a penalty, you must avoid the circumstance or prevent it.

After the duration of a Prediction, circumstances change so that it’s no longer relevant and it vanishes (unless it’s permanent, in which case, tough luck).

Modifying Fortune

A Seer can weaken a Prediction to make it more enduring, or shorten it to increase its potency.

  • You can alter the duration of a Prediction by reducing it’s Bonus/Penalty by 1 for each time category you want to boost it.

  • Alternatively, you can reduce it’s time category to increase it’s Bonus/Penalty by +/-1 per step.

For example, a Rank 9 Prophecy could be permanent if it only enforced a -1 Effort Penalty, or it could last but a single week and enforce a crippling -5!

Auspicious Places and Things

When interacting with auspicious inanimate things, like places or objects which carry a Prediction Imbalance, it is your actions, rather than the subjects, that determine whether you can claim the bonus or avoid the penalty.

For example, if you’re battling at Garbage Dump Paradise and dealing with its eternal Prediction Imbalance “Those who do harm to their loved ones here will prosper”, then you can claim its juicy +3 Effort bonus during any round in which you’re attempting to injure somebody you love. This has led to more than one bitter martial rivalry ending in marriage, by the way, so use this strategy judiciously.

The Limits of Prophecy

Every subject may only be under a single Prediction Imbalance and a single Prophecy at a given time. The highest- Ranked of these are the only ones which stick; lesser Prophecies and Predictions revealing only incomplete, garbled or inaccurate visions of fate.

system.description: Due to their simian anatomy, baboon-men can brachiate and climb at Agility 4 as their move action.

Collectively, they can practice the Art of the Sage due to the esoteric teachings of their religion. Requires a huge amount of them and every action is a ritual that takes hours or days at specific times and equinoxes to work; this uses the Platoon rules.
Can use Ferocity for Senses actions
Horses do not have these.
Once the shell is punctured by an attack sufficient to deal damage, it shatters and reduces the armor to 4.
Destructive.
Burrows through sand at Rank 3.

Rakshasa can alter their bodies and appearance at will, doubling or halving their overall mass through magic. They can also turn into any natural desert animal, but if it’s smaller or larger than their “half or double” boundary then they become a large or small enough version to fit within those parameters.

system.powers:
Buried in moldering tomes and kept in secret vaults in hell are the ancient laws of demonkind. They contain the words of command for the dead and for devils, the rituals by which they may be bound in service and commanded. This deep magic was laid down in antediluvian antiquity so that the high cosmos was not subject to the petty bickering and power-grabs that plague the elemental courts, but they came with a cost; any one versed in their nuances could evoke and claim their sovereignty. The sorcerer's art was thieved from hell one lifetime at a time, its cost paid in blood and souls.

Uses the Spirit skill.

New Action: Command the Dead

With an hour-long ritual, an imperious command and a fresh supply of bodies, you raise the dead to do your bidding. The Rank of your Spirit action determines the quality and amount of the undead.

  • Rank 3: You raise a single human or animal corpse, even one withered entirely into bones. It follows your commands but is about as intelligent and obedient as a barely-tamed, hungry wolf. It has a Ferocity of 1.If fed with a steady supply of living flesh and trained, it gains a measure of sentience; this turns its Ferocity into Effort and it can become a Disciple after 1 Plot Arc.

  • Rank 6: You can bestow a single corpse with sentience and self-control, making a Ghoul, an intelligent undead servant of impressive skill. In addition to an Effort of 2, they have a single Mortal Mastery of your choosing, 2 total Health Levels, a Focus Slot and access to their Hell Chakra. They are created with Loyalty 10, but this can erode as usual. Protip: they eat copious volumes of fresh meat. They may be trained as Disciples act in all respects like selfish, cannibalistic Minor Heroes.

  • Rank 9: You may imbue a corpse with not only intelligence and will, but mystical power. You can recreate any undead of your choosing of Effort/Ferocity 10 or less.

  • Rank 12: Your dark mastery now allows you to create undead of Effort/Ferocity up to 20.

  • Rank 14+: You can create an undead being of up to Effort/ Ferocity 30. Additionally, you can remove your own heart and transform yourself into an undead creature.

Becoming Eternal

If you turn yourself undead, your corpse-body operates by the following rules:

  • You neither age nor die.

  • You can neither be poisoned nor become sick (although your body can be the vector of sickness for others).

They twist fate, rather than your body; suppressing them requires intense acts of will, constant adherence to weird behavior, or some other distracting practice that reduces your available Effort. If you want access to your full Effort, the world starts to warp around you as your new destiny manipulates circumstances to manifest itself.

Elemental Blessings

Alternatively, you can place an Elemental Blessing on yourself or any ally. A person may only be under the Influence of a single Blessing.

system.powers:
The future is anyone’s game; people do regrettably have free will, and every problem in history is the result of that cosmic oversight. But the shape of the future is as concrete as the shape of the past, to those who understand how to see it. Some consult venerable poetry-texts, some stick hot pokers into tortoise shells, some toss the ol’ bones or draw from a deck of cards; some are just super-geniuses who figure it out. Whatever the method, these clairvoyants and savants make predictions that come true; where do you think all those ominous prophecies come from?

Uses the Senses Skill

Foretell Prophecy

You make predictions about the future, sensing the subtle twitches of the skein of fate. Prophecies might be somewhat broad and a touch vague, but they’re still true; or, rather, they’re the most likely shape the future will take.

To Foretell a Prophecy, first consult your preferred scrying equipment for ten minutes and craft a Prophecy.

You can (and should) be exceptionally weird and vague with the specifics of your prophecy, but you must articulate an Approach within it that allows cunning actors to exploit fate to their benefit (and avoid its perils!)

Prophecy Approach

The Approach is a statement of the form “The (Situation) must be approached in (Manner)”.

This will serve as the basis for judging whether people are acting in accordance with the Prophecy, similarly to a Dramatic Penalty in other Imbalances.

  • The Situation refers to a forthcoming Scene; it might be a battle, or an important ritual, or a social event; really, any specific event that’s going to happen within this Campaign Arc. While the scene lasts, the Prophecy effects everyone present and everyone whose actions influence the Scene. This means that even distant and indirect actors are affected while interacting with the prophesied event.

  • The Manner that it can be approached is prescriptive, like “cautiously” or “recklessly” or even something more esoteric like “reverently”. This is the trigger that is used to determine if a given character’s actions will be helped/hindered by the Prophecy. It can be as specific or broad as the Seer wishes; specificity will make it harder for foes to take advantage of the Prophecy, but will hinder the freedom of allies to pursue it creatively. Broader Manners allow for more flexibility, but risk the enemy benefiting from your Prophecy.

Next, take a Senses action to determine how accurate, broad and binding your new Prophecy turns out.

While in the Situation, characters must adhere to the Method of the Prophecy to claim its advantages, or avoid its penalties:

  • Rank 1: Adhering to the Manner prescribed for the Prophecy grants Advantage.

  • Rank 3: Additionally, ignoring the Manner causes Disadvantage.

  • Rank 6: Adhering additionally grants you +3 Effort per round. The GM has veto action against your actions while you enjoy this advantage; should a proposed action not harmonize with the Manner, you may not take that action.

  • Rank 9: Ignoring the Manner now additionally penalizes you -3 Effort each round. The GM must warn you, prior to committing to an action, if it will carry this auspicious sanction. If you cannot be penalized during this round, then you will lose 3 Effort in a future round/action of the GM’s choosing instead. Fate is cruel!

  • Rank 12: The scope of your Prophecy is broadened and deepened. It now applies more generally; the Prediction remains for the entire next Campaign Arc and influences everyone whose actions can be traced to the Situation during that time.

  • Rank 14+: Your Prophecy becomes permanent; it is inherited by the descendants of those involved in the situation, or the place it is foretold to occur, forever predicting those bloodlines or areas as auspicious places for the Situation to take place

Example Prophecies

Example Prophecy 1: “When the sun rises, everyone weeps. The air of winter is foul. The southern mountain has a bird and the north is fallen. When the cock crows, the sun shall set.”

Approach: The forthcoming battle in the Sword Peak Mountains must be approached subtly

Rank: 9

In this example, an indirect, stealthy or otherwise subtle approach to battle would be in accordance with the Approach.

Example Prophecy 2: “God is blind. The grass and trees grow downward. Positive and negative switch positions. Up is earth, and down is Heaven. Even the headless must wear crimson caps. Abusing authority, when will this end? A history of countless blunders will ensue”

Approach: The governance of Thankless Toil Providence must be approached frugally

Rank: 12

A more powerful Prophecy, this one applies to the entire next Campaign Arc, rather than a single scene. It essentially forbids ill-considered actions on the part of the rulers of the Thankless Toil Domain, forcing them to act uncharacteristically wise in their stewardship, the morons.

Predict Fate

You can foretell the fate of any person, place or thing, seeing their future as clearly as their present. These predictions are more concrete and limited in scope, so are much faster to generate; merely glance at your scrying tool and consider the subject and in a heartbeat the truth will reveal itself to you.

Predicting Fate creates an special kind of Imbalance, called a Prediction Imbalance. These are stranger than normal Imbalances, and can be applied to anything, not just people. They can also influence how others interact with the subject, rather than simply dictating how the subject will act.

To create a Prediciton Imbalance, use a Senses action and make a brief prediction using your chosen divination method, directed towards any a person, place or thing. You need not be able to perceive the target directly, as your divination sees their fate, rather than the subject itself.

Your prediction must take the form of: “(Subject) will (Prosper/Decline) if (Circumstance arises)”

  • For nonliving targets, the Rank of your action determines the Rank of the Prediction.

  • For living targets, they may defend against your prophesied doom with their own Senses action, subtracting their action from yours and taking Aggravation equal to the difference.

You may choose whether the target Prospers or Declines.

Prosper predictions allow the target to claim a Bonus if their actions this round/turn all adhere to the prophecy’s dictates.

Decline predictions enforce their Penalty unless their target adheres to the prophecy’s edicts this round/turn (in this way, it functions almost identically to a Dramatic Penalty)

Note that Predictions Imbalances need not adhere strictly to the “Subject will decline/prosper if circumstance” formula, they need merely contain a subject, action and direction of fortunes. So “Those who swear the Pumpkin-Stealing Oath will decline if they betray its dictates” works as well as “Those who break the Pumpkin-Stealing Oath shall suffer”

Prediction Imbalances

The Rank of these peculiar Imbalances determine how much of bonus/Penalty they enforce as well as how long they last;

  • Rank 3: +/-1 Effort, 1 Week

  • Rank 6: +/-2 Effort, 1 Month

  • Rank 9: +/-3 Effort, 1 Season/Arc

  • Rank 12: +/-4 Effort, 1 Year

  • Rank 14+: +/-5 Effort, Permanent

Prosper predictions award Effort bonuses, while Decline predictions enforce penalties. To claim a bonus, you must either act within or cause the described circumstance. To avoid a penalty, you must avoid the circumstance or prevent it.

After the duration of a Prediction, circumstances change so that it’s no longer relevant and it vanishes (unless it’s permanent, in which case, tough luck).

Modifying Fortune

A Seer can weaken a Prediction to make it more enduring, or shorten it to increase its potency.

  • You can alter the duration of a Prediction by reducing it’s Bonus/Penalty by 1 for each time category you want to boost it.

  • Alternatively, you can reduce it’s time category to increase it’s Bonus/Penalty by +/-1 per step.

For example, a Rank 9 Prophecy could be permanent if it only enforced a -1 Effort Penalty, or it could last but a single week and enforce a crippling -5!

Auspicious Places and Things

When interacting with auspicious inanimate things, like places or objects which carry a Prediction Imbalance, it is your actions, rather than the subjects, that determine whether you can claim the bonus or avoid the penalty.

For example, if you’re battling at Garbage Dump Paradise and dealing with its eternal Prediction Imbalance “Those who do harm to their loved ones here will prosper”, then you can claim its juicy +3 Effort bonus during any round in which you’re attempting to injure somebody you love. This has led to more than one bitter martial rivalry ending in marriage, by the way, so use this strategy judiciously.

The Limits of Prophecy

Every subject may only be under a single Prediction Imbalance and a single Prophecy at a given time. The highest- Ranked of these are the only ones which stick; lesser Prophecies and Predictions revealing only incomplete, garbled or inaccurate visions of fate.

system.powers:
Masters of technology and innovation, the Artisan dares the mystical principles of invention and industry that lesser methods required aeons to recreate. Their craft is the art, philosophy and tradition of science, unclouded by the prejudice of intellectual bias. They align their inventiveness and engineering with the divine principles of creation, allowing them to make miracles of craftsmanship.

Uses the Intellect skill.

New Action: Kludge

You can repair anything. Anything.

Granted a single action, a malfunctioning or broken device, some tools and some makeshift materials for repair, you can render a broken piece of machinery temporarily operational. This is extraordinarily dangerous to both the machine and its user, but in a pinch, sometimes, you risk it.

  • Requires an Intellect action, which may be during an action scene as you frantically repair a device in the blink of an eye.

  • You must have tools which could possibly allow you to operate on the machine. They might be slipshod and improvised, but they need to be able to get the job done.

  • You must have some reasonably appropriate scrap materials to be used in the repair. Keep in mind that, in the real actual world, a radiator can be temporarily repaired with an egg,

  • You must have a broken machine in need of fixing. Note that, every System or Weapon on a vehicle counts as a single machine, as does the Vehicle itself.

If all of the above criteria are met, you may attempt to Kludge the machine back into hazardous life.

The Rank of your Intellect action determines the sophistication of the machine you can repair. If you have the wits to engineer a tool of equal or greater sophistication than the one you are Kludging, then you miraculously repair the machine… Sort of.

Every time the machine is operated, roll a d10 atfer using it to determine if it malfunctions.

1 or less: It explodes catastrophically, with a Rank equal to the Rank required to repair it (more technology makes bigger booms, it’s a universal law).

2-3: It breaks down once again, this time beyond repair.

4-10: Despite all odds, it operates normally

Every time the machine is used, subtract a cumulative -1 from the next roll. At the end of the current scene, a Kludged machine falls apart into worthless scrap and may never be repaired again.

New Action: Engineer Machine Servant

You can do with science what is typically accomplished only through magic: Your use of Intellect has the following new functions at these Ranks:

Rank 3: You can engineer an unintelligent but otherwise sophisticated robot servitor. They obey your direct commands and perform simple tasks. They require no food nor water nor air and are powered for decades by their brass and crystal hearts. They are incredibly strong and resilient, able to lift up to Power 4 and withstand hardship up to Endurance 4, but they are clumsy and operate at Agility 0. Its Ferocity is 1, as a standard human sans intelligence.

The device is endowed with both intelligence and personality; it has an identity, opinions, a perspective, feelings, the whole nine yards. Its effective Intellect is Rank 4. If given to a humanoid machine, its Effort is effectively 2. Rank 9: You can construct a mighty behemoth of piston and steel. It can be as hulking as a tank (Size 7) and has Ferocity 12. You can engineer weaponry and motility for them that is equivalent in potency to a Beast-Tier creature.

Rank 12: You may endow an intelligent mechanical servitor with incredible capabilities through the installation of a Prana Battery. Each Battery operates like a Chakra, with an Elemental Alignment (Earth, Fire, Water, etc.), a Pool of 3 and Recovery of 6. You may program any Techniques you know into your servitor’s steel brain, allowing them to make use of this artificial martial magic. Due to structural limitation (ie; the total lack of an actual soul), these devices cannot Prana Flare.

Rank 14+: You can create a technological demigod. It can be as hulking as a tank and operates with an Effort of 15-20. It is installed with 7 Prana batteries and programmed with any Techniques you know. Although perfectly loyal to you, it has its own drive and desires and pursues them with all the powers at its disposal.

Engineering a miracle requires 1 frantic night’s worth of mad invention and construction in the case of Rank 3-9, and 1 Week’s tireless engineering for Rank 12+.

Constructing miraculous inventions requires a well-stocked laboratory sanctified to the elements (Wealth 1000 and a Rank 4 Spirit action must be used in it’s construction at a minimum).

Construction otherwise follows all the normal Crafting rules (p.17). All miraculous construction requires one-third of its materials as Magic Resources.

New Action: Awaken A. I.

You can endow an appropriately sophisticated computer with Artificial Intelligence that is as real and conscious as a spiritual being. The Rank of Intellect you achieve generates an A.I. of equal power to a being summoned through an equivalent Spirit action.

It has Effort and powers equivalent to these beings, but it must remain within the technological confines of its computer universe, making it effectively Ghostly (p.185). It may communicate through and operate all of the devices connected to it’s processor, but it cannot use it’s powers in any other physical capacity.

system.powers:
The courtier learns the language of the soul; those bottomless, emotional wavelengths that direct our actions more powerfully than reason can dare. They neither pull strings nor play games; they are machinists, delicately carving human personalities into interlocking shapes for their grand designs. Theirs is a subtle, insidious art; they sow memetics into their victims and reap a bountiful harvest of passion; much like the farmer, they know how to plant for the crop they desire.

Uses the Heart skill.

New Action: Stoke Passion

Courtiers can provoke a powerful, sustained attitude in the heart of another. Say something in-character to manipulate your target and take a Heart action. This can be defended against with Heart, as the foe counter-argues or rebukes your manipulations to the best of their ability. If your rhetoric overcomes theirs, the “damage” of your attack generates Aggravation towards an Emotional Imbalance as you fill their heart with poisonous magic.

You may Stoke Passions even in the midst of combat; a few quick but well-positioned words are more than enough to throw someone into a rage or kindle their deepest suspicions.

Choose the subject of the target’s Imbalance (a person, place, idea, plan, relationship, anything someone might feel passionately about) and choose one of the Seven Classic Emotions to inflame. These weak points of the soul are what Courtiers exploit to create their persistent manipulations.

Bending the Emperor’s Ear

A whisper in the right ear can change the fate of nations. Courtiers, with their encyclopedic understanding of human social dynamics and organizations of power, are masters of influencing the ideas of key decision-makers to their benefit. This allows them to orchestrate the Domain-level actions undertaken by their Rulers. Take a Heart action, targeting either the Ruler or one of their advisors or confidants. The Rank of your action determines how comprehensive your manipulations are:

  • Rank 1: 1 Domain action; may be a single die.

  • Rank 3: 1 Domain action, must be a Rank 2+ action if available.

  • Rank 6: 1 Domain action, must be their highest-Ranked action.

  • Rank 9: 2 Domain actions, their Highest-Ranked and one additional.

  • Rank 12: 3 Domain actions, each which must be the highest available.

  • Rank 14+: Their entire turn is spent according to the courtier’s wishes.

Insidiously, the Ruler is unaware that they are acting out the Courtier’s machinations and in fact, believe themselves to be following their own ideas and desires. An equal-Ranked Heart action can uncover the deception and return their true will to them.

Healing Emotional Trauma

Due to your extensive knowledge of the human heart and your delicacy at manipulating the psyche, you are able to heal the traumas and phobias of others. You may treat one patient per Effortless Rank. After a month-long period of psychoanalysis and therapy, apply a Heart action to each patient. They heal emotional injury at an advanced rate according to the Rank of action used to treat them:

  • Rank 3: 2d10 Emotional Aggravation

  • Rank 6: 3d10 Emotional Aggravation

  • Rank 9: 4d10 Emotional Aggravation

  • Rank 12: 1d10 Ranks of Emotional Imbalance

  • Rank 14+: 2d10 Ranks of Emotional Imbalance
